'''Philip John Siemens''' (November 13, 1943 – June 29, 2023) was a theoretical physicist who trained at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] and [[Cornell University|Cornell]], and who taught and conducted research at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]], [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], [[Texas A&M University]], [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]], and [[Oregon State University]].

He was a fellow of both the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].
== Early life and education ==
Philip John Siemens, the eldest of Dorothea and Jacob J. Siemens' five children, was born November 13, 1943, in [[Elgin, Illinois]]. He attended [[Wheaton Academy]] and earned a [[National Merit Scholarship Program|National Merit scholarship]]<ref>{{Cite news |date=1961-03-16 |title=3 at Wheaton Academy Get Merit Honors |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/chicago-tribune-3-at-wheaton-academy-get/200040810/ |access-date=2026-06-22 |work=Chicago Tribune |pages=40}}</ref> to study at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where he majored in physics.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-11-09 |title=Philip John Siemens Obituary - Eugene Register-Guard |url=https://registerguard.com/obituaries/pore0622836 |access-date=2026-05-30 |website=registerguard.com |language=en}}</ref> 

As a [[Cornell University]] graduate student, Siemens specialized in theoretical nuclear physics. He co-authored two publications prior to his dissertation: in 1967, "Shape of Heavy Nuclei",<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Siemens |first1=Philip J. |last2=Bethe |first2=H. A. |date=1967-04-24 |title=Shape of Heavy Nuclei |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.18.704 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en-US |volume=18 |issue=17 |pages=704–706 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.18.704 |bibcode=1967PhRvL..18..704S |issn=0031-9007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812044613/https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.18.704 |archive-date=2024-08-12}}</ref> and in 1969, "Nuclear-matter reaction matrix".<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Siemens |first1=Philip J. |last2=Bethe |first2=H. A. |date=1967-04-24 |title=Shape of Heavy Nuclei |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.18.704 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=18 |issue=17 |pages=704–706 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.18.704 |bibcode=1967PhRvL..18..704S |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

His 1970 dissertation, ''New Statistical Theory of the Nuclear Surface,'' was advised by Nobel laureate [[Hans Bethe]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Siemens |first=Philip J. |date=January 1970 |title=New Statistical Theory of the Nuclear Surface. I |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/66167 |access-date=2026-06-20 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.1.98|journal= Physical Review C|volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=98–111 |bibcode=1970PhRvC...1...98S }}</ref>

== Career ==
In the decade following completion of his doctorate, Siemens worked at the University of Copenhagen's [[Niels Bohr Institute]]. In 1975, he co-authored, "Linear response theory for dissipation in heavy-ion collisions" with Helmut Hofmann.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hofmann |first1=Helmut |last2=Siemens |first2=Philip J. |date=22 April 1975 |title=Linear response theory for dissipation in heavy-ion collisions |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0375947476904814 |journal=Nuclear Physics A |language=en |volume=257 |issue=1 |pages=165–188 |doi=10.1016/0375-9474(76)90481-4|url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

While on leave from the Niels Bohr Institute in 1979, Siemens also co-authored three papers with Joseph I. Kapusta at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]: "Evidence for a Soft Nuclear-Matter Equation of State",<ref name="auto">{{Cite journal |last1=Siemens |first1=Philip J. |last2=Kapusta |first2=Joseph I. |date=1979-11-12 |title=Evidence for a Soft Nuclear-Matter Equation of State |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.1486 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en-US |volume=43 |issue=20 |pages=1486–1489 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.1486 |bibcode=1979PhRvL..43.1486S |issn=0031-9007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260310133729/https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.1486 |archive-date=2026-03-10}}</ref> "Evidence for a Blast Wave from Compressed Nuclear Matter",<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Siemens |first1=Philip J. |last2=Rasmussen |first2=John O. |date=1979-04-02 |title=Evidence for a Blast Wave from Compressed Nuclear Matter |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.42.880 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en-US |volume=42 |issue=14 |pages=880–883 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.42.880 |bibcode=1979PhRvL..42..880S |issn=0031-9007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251121093352/https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.42.880 |archive-date=2025-11-21}}</ref> and "Evidence for a Soft Nuclear-Matter Equation of State".<ref name="auto"/>

In the 1980s, Siemens was recruited to establish [[Texas A&M University System|Texas A&M University's]] Physics Department and Cyclotron Institute faculty.<ref name=":0" /> While there between 1983 and 1985, he authored and co-authored four studies: "Liquid–gas phase transition in nuclear matter",<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Siemens |first=Philip J. |date=September 1983 |title=Liquid–gas phase transition in nuclear matter |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/305410a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=305 |issue=5933 |pages=410–412 |doi=10.1038/305410a0 |bibcode=1983Natur.305..410S |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> "Nuclear fragmentation",<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bertsch |first1=G. |last2=J. Siemens |first2=Philip |date=June 1983 |title=Nuclear fragmentation |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0370269383900047 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en-US |volume=126 |issue=1–2 |pages=9–12 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(83)90004-7 |bibcode=1983PhLB..126....9B |issn=0370-2693 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231222034920/https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0370269383900047 |archive-date=2023-12-22|url-access=subscription }}</ref> "Testing QCD Plasma Formation by Pion Correlations in Relativistic Nuclear Collisions",<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lopez |first1=Jorge A. |last2=Parikh |first2=Jitendra C. |last3=Siemens |first3=Philip J. |date=1984-09-24 |title=Testing QCD Plasma Formation by Pion Correlations in Relativistic Nuclear Collisions |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.1216 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=53 |issue=13 |pages=1216–1218 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.1216 |bibcode=1984PhRvL..53.1216L |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and "Testing of QCD Plasma Formation by Dilepton Spectra in Relativistic Nuclear Collisions".<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Siemens |first1=Philip J. |last2=Chin |first2=Siu A. |date=1985-09-16 |title=Testing of QCD Plasma Formation by Dilepton Spectra in Relativistic Nuclear Collisions |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.1266 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=55 |issue=12 |pages=1266–1268 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.1266 |pmid=10031772 |bibcode=1985PhRvL..55.1266S |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  

Siemens was welcomed as a "distinguished scientist" at [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]] in 1986.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1986-02-15 |title=A warm welcome |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-knoxville-news-sentinel-a-warm-welco/200042520/ |access-date=2026-06-22 |work=The Knoxville News-Sentinel |pages=6}}</ref> The Knoxville ''News Sentinel'' reported Siemens was "recognized as one of the theoretical leaders in the physics of nuclei heated to very high temperatures stellar explosions and in high-energy collisions."<ref>{{Cite news |date=1986-02-14 |title=3 scientists appointed to UT, ORNL |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-knoxville-news-sentinel-3-scientists/200042817/ |access-date=2026-06-22 |work=[[The Knoxville News-Sentinel]] |pages=26 }}</ref> ''The Tomahawk'' in [[Mountain City, Tennessee|Mountain City]] called Siemens "a recognized leader in the theoretical interpretation of nuclear structures and collisions of energetic heavy nuclei produced by large particle accelerators".<ref>{{Cite news |date=1986-05-28 |title=Distinguished scientists join university staff |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-tomahawk-distinguished-scientists-jo/200041313/ |access-date=2026-06-22 |work=The Tomahawk |pages=11}}</ref>

While at the [[University of Tennessee]] in the late 1980s, Siemens published two studies: "Bubbles and drops in superheated and supercooled nuclear matter,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Li |first1=Bao-An |last2=Pratt |first2=Scott |last3=Siemens |first3=Philip J. |date=1988-04-01 |title=Bubbles and drops in superheated and supercooled nuclear matter |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevC.37.1473 |journal=Physical Review C |language=en |volume=37 |issue=4 |pages=1473–1477 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.37.1473 |pmid=9954600 |bibcode=1988PhRvC..37.1473L |issn=0556-2813|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and "Color correlations in QCD plasma".<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Parikh |first1=Jitendra C. |last2=Siemens |first2=Philip J. |date=1988-06-01 |title=Color correlations in QCD plasma |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.37.3246 |journal=Physical Review D |language=en |volume=37 |issue=11 |pages=3246–3251 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.37.3246 |pmid=9958615 |bibcode=1988PhRvD..37.3246P |issn=0556-2821|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He also co-authored the 1989 publication of "Relativistic transport theory of fluctuating fields for hadrons".<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Siemens |first1=Philip J. |last2=Soyeur |first2=Madeleine |last3=White |first3=Gary D. |last4=Lantto |first4=Lauri J. |last5=Davies |first5=K. Thomas R. |date=1989-12-01 |title=Relativistic transport theory of fluctuating fields for hadrons |url=https://journals.aps.org/prc/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevC.40.2641 |journal=Physical Review C |language=en-US |volume=40 |issue=6 |pages=2641–2671 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.40.2641 |pmid=9966276 |bibcode=1989PhRvC..40.2641S |issn=0556-2813 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419055225/https://journals.aps.org/prc/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevC.40.2641 |archive-date=2024-04-19}}</ref>

Near the end of his career, wanting to be closer to his family in Oregon, he "convinced [[Oregon State University]] in [[Corvallis, Oregon|Corvallis]] to hire him and increase its commitment to theoretical physics".<ref name=":0" /> In 1990 he co-authored "Truncation of Schwinger-Dyson equations and the 1/𝑁 expansion in the O⁡(𝑁) model",<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Korpa |first1=C. L. |last2=Parikh |first2=Jitendra C. |last3=Siemens |first3=Philip J. |date=1990-02-15 |title=Truncation of Schwinger-Dyson equations and the 1 N expansion in the O ( N ) model |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.41.1276 |journal=Physical Review D |language=en |volume=41 |issue=4 |pages=1276–1279 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.41.1276 |pmid=10012463 |bibcode=1990PhRvD..41.1276K |issn=0556-2821|url-access=subscription }}</ref> followed by two papers in 1991: "Vaporization of color-singlet pairs from a quark-gluon plasma",<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Vischer |first1=Axel P. |last2=Parikh |first2=Jitendra C. |last3=Siemens |first3=Philip J. |date=1991-01-01 |title=Vaporization of color-singlet pairs from a quark-gluon plasma |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.43.271 |journal=Physical Review D |language=en |volume=43 |issue=1 |pages=271–273 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.43.271 |pmid=10013256 |bibcode=1991PhRvD..43..271V |issn=0556-2821|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and "Model solutions of regularized relativistic transport equations".<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Milana |first1=Joseph P. |last2=Siemens |first2=Philip J. |date=1991-05-01 |title=Model solutions of regularized relativistic transport equations |url=https://journals.aps.org/prc/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevC.43.2377 |journal=Physical Review C |language=en-US |volume=43 |issue=5 |pages=2377–2392 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.43.2377 |pmid=9967288 |bibcode=1991PhRvC..43.2377M |issn=0556-2813 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220301155844/https://journals.aps.org/prc/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevC.43.2377 |archive-date=2022-03-01}}</ref> These papers were followed by three more: "Kaon pictures of QCD plasma droplets"<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Pratt |first1=Scott |last2=Siemens |first2=Philip J. |last3=Vischer |first3=Axel P. |date=1992-02-24 |title=Kaon pictures of QCD plasma droplets |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.68.1109 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=68 |issue=8 |pages=1109–1111 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.68.1109 |pmid=10046082 |bibcode=1992PhRvL..68.1109P |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription }}</ref> in 1992; "Crossing-symmetric two-particle reduction of four-point vertex"<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Korpa |first1=C. L. |last2=Siemens |first2=Philip J. |date=1993-06-01 |title=Crossing-symmetric two-particle reduction of four-point vertex |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevC.47.2481 |journal=Physical Review C |language=en |volume=47 |issue=6 |pages=2481–2484 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.47.2481 |pmid=9968721 |bibcode=1993PhRvC..47.2481K |issn=0556-2813|url-access=subscription }}</ref> in 1993; and "Self-consistent couplings of pions and Δ-hole states in nuclear matter"<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Xia |first1=Linhua |last2=Siemens |first2=Philip J. |last3=Soyeur |first3=Madeleine |date=October 1994 |title=Self-consistent couplings of pions and Δ-hole states in nuclear matter |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0375947494907579 |journal=Nuclear Physics A |language=en |volume=578 |issue=3–4 |pages=493–510 |doi=10.1016/0375-9474(94)90757-9 |bibcode=1994NuPhA.578..493X |url-access=subscription }}</ref> in 1994. 

Philip Siemens' retirement was acknowledged in the department newsletter in January 2007.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jansen |first=Henri |date=January 2007 |title=Letter From the Chair |url=https://physics.oregonstate.edu/sites/physics.oregonstate.edu/files/2022-10/Newsletter%202006.pdf |access-date=24 June 2007 |work=OSU Physics Newsletter}}</ref> He died of [[leukemia]] in [[Eugene, Oregon|Eugene]] in January 2023.<ref name=":0" />

== Honors ==

* 1984 Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], Dvision of Nuclear Physics, cited ''For important contributions to the theory of many-body systems as applied to nuclear physics.''<ref>{{Cite web |date=1984 |title=APS Fellows Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=Philip%20Siemens&af=true |access-date=May 29, 2026}}</ref>

* 1991 Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], for achievements in ''"''theoretical studies of nuclear matter, the nuclear equation of state and the physics of nuclear collision''"''.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1991-03-13 |title=OSU scientists honored |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/corvallis-gazette-times-osu-scientists-h/200039673/ |access-date=2026-06-22 |work=Corvallis Gazette-Times |pages=2}}</ref>
